question: Should the experimental Claws lifecycle stack expose this versioned core `claws update` planning and consent contract now, before the prerequisite diagnostics and follow-on apply PRs have landed?
rationale: This is a new core lifecycle product surface with persistent ownership semantics, a public CLI contract, and a planned mutation consumer; implementation review cannot decide its long-term ownership or rollout sequencing.

options.title: Sponsor the bounded core planner
options.body: Approve this read-only, experiment-gated planning contract as the core foundation, then require final-head live proof before merge.

options.title: Pause the stack for RFC resolution
options.body: Keep the PR open but defer merge until the RFC or owner decision settles whether grouped Claws lifecycle management belongs in core.

options.title: Narrow to reusable primitives
options.body: Ask for the generic planning/consent primitives to be separated from Claws-specific CLI and ownership policy before reconsidering the feature.

recommendation.title: Sponsor the bounded core planner
recommendation.body: Approve this read-only, experiment-gated planning contract as the core foundation, then require final-head live proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: He is assigned to the PR and has already defined the key lifecycle and authoritative-preview requirements.
